newsitem.title: UK: Cruise Holdings to seek 'substantial' Oslo IPO.
newsitem.headline: Cruise Holdings to seek 'substantial' Oslo IPO.

text.p: Cruise Holdings Ltd told Reuters on Monday that it intended to seek a "substantial" initial public offering on the Oslo stock market within the next six months.
Larry Magnan, Cruise Holdings president and chief executive officer, said the Miami-based cruise shipping company would also seek a secondary listing on a U.S. exchange.
"Realistically, if we don't do it between now and the end of the year, it will probably be in the first quarter of next year," Magnan told Reuters.
Cruise Holdings previously said it would seek a listing within a year of its June completion of a $14 million private placement.

"The private placement was so enthusiastically received, we are now talking about a listing sooner than planned," Magnan said. "We are meeting with our advisers Enskilda Securities next week in Oslo to discuss that subject as related to timing.
"I cannot give you an exact date, because until I talk to our advisers we are not sure."
Magnan declined to comment on how much cash the firm would try to raise.

"It is hard to tell," he said. "This is one of the reasons we are talking to our advisers. We would like to go out for a substantial equity placement. But just exactly what that would be at this point in time would be speculation.
"I think we would look for a secondary market listing as well, either on Wall Street, or one of the other U.S. exchanges."
Magnan said new cash would be spent on reinforcing its niche owning and operating 'classic' older cruise liners for the mass market.
"One of the reasons we are going public is to raise some money for a war chest," Magnan said.
